name: Celecoxib
indications: Osteoarthritis, Rheumatoid arthritis, Familial adenomatous polyposis
description: A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug that selectively inhibits COX-2, reducing inflammation with theoretically lower GI risk.

name: Hydroxyurea
indications: Sickle cell anemia, Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), Polycythemia vera
description: An antimetabolite that prevents DNA synthesis; frequently used to reduce pain crises in sickle cell disease.

name: Methoxsalen
side_effects: Photosensitivity, nausea, skin aging, increased skin cancer risk
description: A psoralen derivative used in conjunction with UVA radiation (PUVA therapy) to treat severe skin disorders.

name: Raloxifene hydrochloride
side_effects: Hot flashes, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), leg cramps
description: A SERM that acts as an estrogen agonist in bone but an antagonist in breast tissue.

name: Imatinib mesylate
indications: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST)
side_effects: Fluid retention, periorbital edema, nausea, muscle cramps
description: A revolutionary targeted therapy that specifically inhibits the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase in Philadelphia chromosome-positive CML.

name: Vorinostat
description: A histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor that alters gene expression, inducing apoptosis in cancer cells.

name: Temozolomide
description: An alkylating agent that readily crosses the blood-brain barrier, making it a cornerstone for brain tumor treatment.

name: Teniposide
description: A cell cycle-specific topoisomerase II inhibitor used primarily in pediatric leukemias.

name: Thalidomide
description: An immunomodulatory drug infamous for historical birth defects, now highly restricted and used for specific cancers and leprosy.

name: Daunorubicin hydrochloride
indications: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML), Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)
description: An anthracycline antibiotic that intercalates DNA, primarily used for induction therapy in leukemias.

name: Doxorubicin hydrochloride
side_effects: Dilated cardiomyopathy, myelosuppression, alopecia, red urine
description: A widely used anthracycline known colloquially as the "Red Devil" due to its color and severe side effects.

name: Paclitaxel
indications: Breast cancer, Ovarian cancer, Non-small cell lung cancer
description: A taxane derived from the Pacific yew tree that stabilizes microtubules, preventing cellular division.

name: Etoposide
indications: Testicular cancer, Small cell lung cancer
description: A topoisomerase II inhibitor that causes DNA strand breaks, often combined with platinum agents.

name: Exemestane
side_effects: Hot flashes, joint pain, osteoporosis, fatigue
description: An irreversible, steroidal aromatase inhibitor that prevents the conversion of androgens to estrogens.

name: Zoledronic acid
indications: Multiple myeloma, Bone metastases, Hypercalcemia of malignancy
side_effects: Osteonecrosis of the jaw, renal toxicity, flu-like symptoms
description: A potent bisphosphonate that inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption.

name: Gefitinib
side_effects: Acneiform rash, diarrhea, interstitial lung disease
description: A first-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in lung cancers with specific EGFR mutations.

name: Methotrexate
description: A cornerstone antifolate drug used across oncology and rheumatology; toxicity can be rescued with leucovorin.

name: Abiraterone
description: An androgen biosynthesis inhibitor that blocks CYP17A1, usually given with prednisone to prevent adrenal insufficiency.

name: Docetaxel
indications: Breast cancer, Prostate cancer, Non-small cell lung cancer
side_effects: Neutropenia, fluid retention, peripheral neuropathy, alopecia
description: A potent taxane that prevents microtubule depolymerization, often requiring corticosteroid premedication.

name: Lapatinib ditosylate
side_effects: Diarrhea, hepatotoxicity, rash, decreased left ventricular ejection fraction
description: A dual tyrosine kinase inhibitor that blocks both EGFR and HER2 pathways.

name: Sorafenib tosylate
indications: Hepatocellular carcinoma, Renal cell carcinoma, Thyroid cancer
description: A multikinase inhibitor targeting VEGF, PDGF, and RAF kinases to halt tumor angiogenesis and proliferation.

name: Lenalidomide
description: A thalidomide analog with enhanced immunomodulatory and anti-angiogenic properties, requiring strict REMS prescribing.

name: Bortezomib
side_effects: Peripheral neuropathy, thrombocytopenia, fatigue, GI upset
description: The first therapeutic proteasome inhibitor; it disrupts cellular protein degradation, leading to cancer cell death.

name: Carboplatin
description: A platinum-based alkylating agent similar to cisplatin but with less nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity.

name: Tretinoin
side_effects: Retinoic acid syndrome, dry skin, headache, hepatotoxicity
description: A vitamin A derivative that induces differentiation of leukemic promyelocytes into mature granulocytes.

name: Dactinomycin
description: An antitumor antibiotic that binds DNA and inhibits RNA transcription, primarily used in pediatric solid tumors.

name: Nilotinib
description: A second-generation BCR-ABL inhibitor used for CML, particularly when resistance to imatinib develops.

name: Tamoxifen citrate
side_effects: Hot flashes, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), endometrial cancer risk
description: A SERM that is an estrogen antagonist in the breast but an agonist in the uterus, widely used for breast cancer prevention and treatment.

name: Dasatinib
side_effects: Pleural effusion, myelosuppression, bleeding, fluid retention
description: A highly potent second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting BCR-ABL and SRC families.

name: Vandetanib
description: A kinase inhibitor that targets RET, VEGFR, and EGFR, requiring strict EKG monitoring.

name: Sirolimus
side_effects: Impaired wound healing, hyperlipidemia, myelosuppression, mouth ulcers
description: An mTOR inhibitor (also known as rapamycin) that suppresses T-cell activation; avoids the nephrotoxicity seen in calcineurin inhibitors.

name: Sunitinib
indications: Renal cell carcinoma, Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST)
description: A targeted multikinase inhibitor that restricts tumor blood supply and growth.

name: Romidepsin
description: A cyclic depsipeptide HDAC inhibitor that induces cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in T-cell lymphomas.

name: Vincristine sulfate
side_effects: Peripheral neuropathy, paralytic ileus, alopecia (spares bone marrow)
description: A vinca alkaloid that halts cell division; distinct among chemotherapies for its lack of severe myelosuppression.

name: Everolimus
indications: Breast cancer, Renal cell carcinoma, Neuroendocrine tumors
description: An mTOR inhibitor that blocks a crucial pathway for cell growth and angiogenesis.

name: Axitinib
description: A highly selective, potent VEGFR inhibitor used primarily as second-line therapy for advanced kidney cancer.

name: Crizotinib
indications: Non-small cell lung cancer (ALK or ROS1 positive)
side_effects: Vision disorders, nausea, edema, elevated transaminases
description: A targeted therapy specifically designed for lung cancers driven by ALK or ROS1 gene rearrangements.

name: Vemurafenib
side_effects: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, photosensitivity, arthralgia
description: A targeted inhibitor that interrupts the BRAF/MEK step on the MAP kinase pathway in specific melanomas.

name: Megestrol acetate
description: A synthetic progestin primarily utilized as an appetite stimulant in patients with severe wasting syndromes.

name: Chlorambucil
description: A well-tolerated, oral nitrogen mustard alkylating agent used for indolent lymphomas and leukemias.

name: Ruxolitinib
description: A JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor that reduces spleen size and systemic symptoms in myeloproliferative neoplasms.

name: Cyclophosphamide
indications: Breast cancer, Lymphomas, Leukemias, Autoimmune disorders
description: A versatile alkylating agent; requires aggressive hydration and mesna to prevent toxic bladder damage.

name: Quinacrine hydrochloride
description: An older antimalarial and anthelmintic agent occasionally used in specialized rheumatologic or oncologic contexts.

name: Gemcitabine hydrochloride
indications: Pancreatic cancer, Non-small cell lung cancer, Bladder cancer
description: A nucleoside analog highly effective against solid tumors, often the backbone of pancreatic cancer therapy.

name: Letrozole
side_effects: Hot flashes, joint pain, osteoporosis, fatigue
description: A non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor that aggressively suppresses estrogen levels in postmenopausal women.

name: Azacitidine
description: A hypomethylating agent that restores normal function to genes critical for differentiation and proliferation.

name: Mitoxantrone
description: An anthracenedione similar to doxorubicin but generally with slightly less cardiotoxicity; causes blue discoloration.

name: Capecitabine
description: An oral prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, highly convenient for patients but notoriously causes painful red palms and soles.

name: Cytarabine hydrochloride
side_effects: Myelosuppression, cerebellar toxicity (at high doses), conjunctivitis
description: An antimetabolite (ara-C) central to AML induction regimens; high doses require neurologic monitoring.

name: Carmustine
indications: Brain tumors, Hodgkin lymphoma, Multiple myeloma
side_effects: Delayed profound myelosuppression, pulmonary toxicity, nausea
description: A highly lipophilic nitrosourea alkylating agent that easily crosses the blood-brain barrier.

name: Erlotinib hydrochloride
indications: Non-small cell lung cancer (EGFR mutated), Pancreatic cancer
side_effects: Acneiform rash, diarrhea, fatigue, interstitial lung disease
description: An EGFR inhibitor where the presence and severity of the resulting skin rash often correlates with drug efficacy.

name: Oxaliplatin
description: A platinum compound famous for causing a unique, cold-aggravated neuropathy in the hands and throat.

name: Allopurinol
side_effects: Rash (Stevens-Johnson syndrome risk), hepatotoxicity, GI upset
description: A xanthine oxidase inhibitor crucial for preventing uric acid nephropathy during massive cancer cell destruction.

name: Bleomycin sulfate
side_effects: Pulmonary fibrosis, hyperpigmentation, fever (spares bone marrow)
description: An antibiotic chemotherapeutic uniquely known for severe pulmonary toxicity while completely sparing the bone marrow.

name: 4'-Epiadriamycin
description: Also known as Epirubicin; an epimer of doxorubicin designed to retain efficacy while slightly reducing cardiac risks.

name: Floxuridine
description: A pyrimidine analog usually administered directly into the hepatic artery for targeted treatment of liver metastases.

name: Vinblastine sulfate
description: A vinca alkaloid that causes significantly more myelosuppression but less neurotoxicity than its chemical cousin vincristine.

name: Ifosfamide
description: An analog of cyclophosphamide requiring co-administration with mesna to prevent severe hemorrhagic cystitis.

name: Fulvestrant
side_effects: Injection site pain, hot flashes, bone pain
description: A selective estrogen receptor down-regulator (SERD) that binds to and degrades the estrogen receptor.

name: Topotecan hydrochloride
indications: Ovarian cancer, Small cell lung cancer, Cervical cancer
description: A water-soluble topoisomerase I inhibitor derived from camptothecin.

name: Busulfan
indications: Chronic myeloid leukemia (historical), Stem cell transplant conditioning
side_effects: Pulmonary fibrosis ("busulfan lung"), profound myelosuppression, hyperpigmentation
description: A potent alkylating agent used heavily in preparative regimens for bone marrow transplantation.

name: Anastrozole
description: A non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor that is a standard of care for postmenopausal women with hormone-sensitive breast cancer.

name: Cisplatin
indications: Testicular, Ovarian, Bladder, Lung, and Head/Neck cancers
side_effects: Severe nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, severe nausea/vomiting, peripheral neuropathy
description: A highly effective but toxic platinum agent; requires massive IV hydration to protect the kidneys.

name: Streptozocin
description: A naturally occurring nitrosourea specifically toxic to the beta cells of the pancreas.

name: Melphalan
description: A nitrogen mustard alkylating agent frequently used as high-dose conditioning therapy prior to stem cell transplants.

name: Arsenic trioxide
description: An ancient poison repurposed to induce differentiation and apoptosis in APL, often combined with ATRA.

name: Mercaptopurine
indications: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), Inflammatory bowel disease
description: A purine analog whose metabolism is heavily dependent on TPMT genetics; allopurinol severely increases its toxicity.

name: Fluorouracil
description: A core antimetabolite (5-FU) often given with leucovorin to enhance its binding to thymidylate synthase.

name: Cabazitaxel
description: A next-generation taxane designed specifically to overcome resistance developed against docetaxel.

name: Cladribine
description: A purine analog that is highly toxic to lymphocytes, leading to long-lasting depletion of T-cells and B-cells.

name: Vismodegib
side_effects: Muscle spasms, alopecia, dysgeusia (taste changes), weight loss
description: A first-in-class Hedgehog signaling pathway inhibitor used for advanced or metastatic basal cell skin cancer.

name: Mitomycin
side_effects: Delayed myelosuppression, hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), pulmonary toxicity
description: An antitumor antibiotic that acts as an alkylating agent, often given topically inside the bladder for superficial cancer.

name: Fludarabine
description: A purine analog that severely depletes CD4 T-cells, requiring prophylactic antibiotics against PCP and shingles.

name: Decitabine
description: A hypomethylating agent that incorporates into DNA and inhibits DNA methyltransferase, activating tumor suppressor genes.

name: Clofarabine
side_effects: Myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS)
description: A second-generation purine nucleoside analog designed to incorporate the best features of fludarabine and cladribine.

name: Idarubicin hydrochloride
description: An anthracycline with higher lipophilicity than doxorubicin, increasing cellular uptake in leukemic cells.

name: Vinorelbine tartrate
indications: Non-small cell lung cancer, Breast cancer
side_effects: Neutropenia, peripheral neuropathy, injection site reactions
description: A semi-synthetic vinca alkaloid used widely in lung cancer for its slightly better toxicity profile compared to vinblastine.

name: Thiotepa
indications: Breast, Ovarian, Bladder cancers, Transplant conditioning
description: An alkylating agent that is excreted in sweat, requiring patients to shower frequently to prevent severe chemical skin burns.

name: Thioguanine
description: A purine analog closely related to mercaptopurine, used primarily in remission induction or consolidation in AML.

name: Ixabepilone
description: An epothilone class microtubule stabilizer used when tumors have become resistant to standard taxanes like paclitaxel.

name: Pemetrexed Disodium
description: A multi-targeted antifolate that requires patients to take B12 and folic acid supplements to prevent severe toxicity.

name: Dacarbazine
side_effects: Profound nausea and vomiting, myelosuppression, flu-like syndrome
description: An alkylating agent famous for its severe emetogenic potential; a core component of the ABVD regimen for Hodgkin lymphoma.

name: Mitotane
side_effects: Adrenal insufficiency, CNS toxicity (lethargy), GI upset
description: A direct adrenal cytotoxin related to the pesticide DDT, requiring patients to receive lifelong steroid replacement therapy.

name: 7-Ethyl-10-hydroxycamptothecin
description: Also known as SN-38; the highly active metabolite of irinotecan responsible for both its anti-tumor activity and severe gastrointestinal toxicity.

name: Pazopanib hydrochloride
indications: Renal cell carcinoma, Soft tissue sarcoma
side_effects: Hepatotoxicity, hypertension, diarrhea, hair color changes
description: An angiogenesis inhibitor known to cause depigmentation of the hair and severe liver enzyme elevations.

name: Eribulin mesylate
description: A microtubule dynamics inhibitor structurally derived from a compound found in a marine sea sponge.

name: Bendamustine hydrochloride
description: A unique chemotherapy drug that possesses both the properties of an alkylating agent and a purine analog.
